name: Montenegro
summary: A small mountain state: a principality and kingdom before 1918, then part of Yugoslavia and Serbia and Montenegro, independent again since 2006.

location.value: Western Balkans on the Adriatic; 13,883 km².

terrain.value: High limestone mountains (Durmitor), deep canyons (Tara) and a narrow coast with the Bay of Kotor.

climate.value: Mediterranean on the coast; cold, snowy winters in the mountains.

resources.value: Tourism, bauxite and aluminium, timber and hydropower.

disasters.value: A strong earthquake struck the coast in 1979, damaging Kotor and Budva.

urbanisation.value: About two-thirds urban; Podgorica (about 190,000) is the capital, Cetinje the old royal capital.

migration.value: Many people moved to Serbia or abroad; foreign residents buy coastal property.

economicBase.value: A mostly service-based, upper-middle-income economy; tourism is significant (2.1 million visitors in 2022). The euro is used unilaterally. The “quarter of the economy” share is not on the page.

tradeRoutes.value: Port of Bar and the Belgrade–Bar railway.

moneyAndTax.value: Uses the euro without being in the eurozone (the German mark from 1999, the euro from 2002).

inequality.value: Gap between the richer coast and the poorer north.

governmentType.value: A unitary parliamentary republic with an elected president.

keyRulers.value: The Petrović-Njegoš dynasty gained semi-autonomy in 1696, first as a theocracy and later as a secular principality. The page does not mention Petar II Njegoš or Nikola I. Later and present leaders are not named here.

succession.value: Elections; the long-ruling party lost power in 2020.

stability.value: 55.5% voted for independence from Serbia in 2006, just over the 55% required.

eliteConflict.value: Divisions between pro-Serbian and pro-independence parties.

armyAndTech.value: Small armed forces; NATO member since 2017.

majorWars.value: Wars against the Ottomans; Balkan Wars and First World War (as a kingdom).

territoryChange.value: Independent kingdom until 1918; in Yugoslavia, then with Serbia until 2006.

alliancesRivals.value: Joined NATO on 5 June 2017; uses the euro unilaterally without being in the eurozone.

scienceEducation.value: The University of Montenegro was founded in 1974.

openness.value: Open to tourism and foreign investment.

communicationTransport.value: Coastal and mountain roads; a new motorway section built with Chinese loans (2022).

religion.value: 2023 census: Eastern Orthodox 71.1%, Christian overall 74.9%. The Muslim share is not given in the part of the page read.

languageWriting.value: Montenegrin (very close to Serbian), in Latin or Cyrillic script.

artsArchitecture.value: Venetian old towns of Kotor and Budva; Ostrog Monastery built into a cliff.

socialStructure.value: Montenegrins, Serbs, Bosniaks, Albanians and others.

dailyLife.value: Stone houses and flats; seafood on the coast, lamb and cheese inland.

ideasReligions.value: Orthodox Christianity; long tradition of mountain clans.

colonisation.value: Never fully conquered by the Ottomans; the coast was Venetian (1420–1797), then Austrian (1814–1918).

riseSignals.value: Principality from 13 March 1852 (infobox); recognised as independent at the Congress of Berlin in 1878; a kingdom in 1910.

peakPeriod.value: Kingdom under Nikola I (1910–18); tourism growth since 2006.

declineSignals.value: Absorbed into Yugoslavia in 1918, which ended the old kingdom.

outcome.value: Joined the Kingdom of Yugoslavia on 1 December 1918; the 21 May 2006 referendum chose independence with 55.5%, and parliament declared it on 3 June 2006.
